Repository: Go project (labstack/echo v4) checked out at /echo. Work in /echo.

BUG TO FIX (reported by user): The proxy load balancers panic when the target list is empty, instead of returning nil.

Reproduction:
  rb := middleware.NewRandomBalancer(nil)
  rb.Next(c)   // panics: "panic: invalid argument to Intn"
  rrb := middleware.NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*middleware.ProxyTarget{})
  rrb.Next(c)  // panics: "panic: runtime error: integer divide by zero"
Expected behavior: Next must return nil when there are no targets (so the caller can handle "no target available"), never panic.

Relevant code: /echo/middleware/proxy.go, methods `func (b *randomBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget` and `func (b *roundRobinBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget`.

TASKS:
1. FIRST, before making any edit, run the baseline test suite: `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60` (and if the toolchain complains, try `go vet`/`go build ./...`). Record exactly which tests fail BEFORE any edit, so we know the pre-existing failures. Save that output to /tmp/baseline_tests.txt.
2. Then edit /echo/middleware/proxy.go so that both Next implementations return nil when the balancer has no targets (guard on len(b.targets) == 0, taking care with the mutex/locking used in each method). Do NOT change anything else in the file. Do NOT change the Proxy middleware behavior, do NOT touch any *_test.go file.
3. Verify: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./middleware/... -run 'Proxy|Balancer' -v 2>&1 | tail -40` and also write and run a temporary throwaway test (e.g. /tmp/nilcheck_test.go copied into /echo/middleware/ as a temp file, then DELETED afterwards) that calls NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next(ctx) and NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil).Next(ctx) and asserts nil is returned without panic. Make sure the temp test file is removed at the end so the repo is clean (`cd /echo && git status --porcelain` must show only middleware/proxy.go modified).
4. Run the full suite again: `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60` and compare with the baseline: no test that passed at baseline may fail now.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff of middleware/proxy.go, baseline failing tests, post-fix failing tests, and confirmation that git status shows only middleware/proxy.go modified.

BUG TO FIX (reported by user): When a request does not match any registered route, `echo.Context.Path()` still returns the requested URL path instead of the empty string. `Path()` is documented as returning "the path of the matched route".

Reproduction:
```go
e := echo.New()
e.GET("/users/:id", handler)
e.HTTPErrorHandler = func(err error, c echo.Context) {
    fmt.Println(c.Path()) // requesting /does-not-exist prints "/does-not-exist", expected ""
}
```
Matched requests behave correctly.

TASKS:
1. BEFORE any edit, run the baseline test suite: `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and save to /tmp/baseline2.txt. Record which tests fail at baseline (these are the only ones allowed to fail later).
2. Investigate: look at /echo/router.go (function Find / the not-found path), /echo/echo.go (ServeHTTP, NotFoundHandler, Context#Path / SetPath), /echo/context.go. Find where the context path is set for unmatched requests. Note that the router must still be able to serve the not-found handler correctly, and `c.Path()` must remain correct for matched routes (including for the 405 / method-not-allowed case and for trailing-slash / static routes).
3. Make the MINIMAL fix so that `c.Path()` is empty ("") when no route matched. Be careful: the router's Find() sets the path for the not-found case; check whether any other code depends on it (grep for SetPath, Path(), and any test that asserts Path() on unmatched requests, e.g. in router_test.go or echo_test.go). If a pre-existing test asserts the old behavior for an unmatched route, then DO NOT change the behavior in a way that breaks it — instead report the conflict and leave the code unchanged. Pre-existing green tests must keep passing.
4. Verify with a temporary throwaway test file (e.g. /echo/zz_path_temp_test.go, package echo) that: (a) requesting an unmatched path yields c.Path() == "" inside HTTPErrorHandler; (b) a matched route /users/:id yields "/users/:id"; (c) the not-found response status is still 404 and the error handler is still called. Delete the temp file afterwards.
5. Run the full suite again: `cd /echo && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and compare to baseline: no previously-passing test may fail. Also run `go vet ./...`.
6. `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` must show only the source file(s) you intentionally changed (no temp files).

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, the baseline vs post-fix test results, whether any pre-existing test conflicted with the expected behavior, and confirmation the temp test file is deleted.

BUG TO FIX (reported by user): `echo.Context.Scheme()` (in /echo/context.go, method `func (c *context) Scheme() string`) returns a bogus scheme taken from a request header instead of ignoring it and falling back to the next valid source.

Reproduction:
```go
c.Request().Header.Set("X-Forwarded-Proto", "ftp")
c.Request().Header.Set("X-Url-Scheme", "https")
fmt.Println(c.Scheme()) // prints "ftp", expected "https"
```
Expected: a header value that is not a real/valid scheme (i.e. not "http" or "https") must be ignored, so the next source is consulted (X-Forwarded-Protocol, X-Forwarded-Ssl, X-Url-Scheme), and "http" is the final default. The same validation must apply to all scheme headers consulted by Scheme().

TASKS:
1. BEFORE any edit, run the baseline suite: `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and save to /tmp/baseline3.txt. Record baseline failures (only those may fail later).
2. Read /echo/context.go (Scheme, around line 252) and the `Context` interface documentation for `Scheme()` in the same file. Also grep the repo for other places that read these scheme headers (e.g. /echo/middleware/secure.go uses HeaderXForwardedProto == "https", /echo/middleware/redirect.go) and check whether they need the same treatment — but ONLY change what is needed for the reported bug; do not refactor unrelated code.
3. Implement the minimal fix in /echo/context.go: treat a header value as a valid scheme only when it is "http" or "https" (case-insensitive is reasonable; document your choice). Keep the existing precedence order: TLS -> X-Forwarded-Proto -> X-Forwarded-Protocol -> X-Forwarded-Ssl=="on" -> X-Url-Scheme -> "http".
4. Verify with a temporary throwaway test file (e.g. /echo/zz_scheme_temp_test.go, package echo) covering: (a) X-Forwarded-Proto=ftp + X-Url-Scheme=https -> "https"; (b) X-Forwarded-Proto=ftp with no fallback -> "http"; (c) X-Forwarded-Proto=https -> "https"; (d) X-Forwarded-Protocol=http -> "http"; (e) X-Forwarded-Ssl=on -> "https"; (f) TLS -> "https"; (g) X-Url-Scheme=ftp -> "http". Delete the temp file afterwards.
5. Run the full suite: `cd /echo && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and compare with baseline — no previously passing test may fail (in particular TestContext_Scheme in context_test.go must still pass). Run `go vet ./...`.
6. `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` must show only the source file(s) you intentionally changed (no temp files).

REPORT BACK: exact diff, baseline vs post-fix test results, and confirmation the temp file is deleted.

BUG TO FIX (reported by user): Binding query parameters into a map does not handle repeated keys.

Reproduction:
```go
m := map[string][]string{}
if err := c.Bind(&m); err != nil { return err }
```
For a request like `?tag=a&tag=b`:
- with destination `map[string][]string` it PANICS with `reflect: SetMapIndex: value of type string is not assignable to type []string`
- with destination `map[string]interface{}` it does not panic but each key holds a single string instead of the slice of values
Expected: `m` should be `{"tag": ["a", "b"]}` — every value for a repeated key must be kept.

Relevant code: /echo/bind.go (look for the query-param / form binding code, likely a function that iterates over `values` from `c.QueryParams()` / `url.Values` and sets map entries via reflection, e.g. `bindData`, `bindMap` or similar). Also /echo/binder.go and /echo/context.go for how query params are obtained.

TASKS:
1. BEFORE any edit, run the baseline suite: `cd /echo && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and save to /tmp/baseline4.txt. Record baseline failures (only those may fail later).
2. Read /echo/bind.go fully and understand how maps are bound. Then implement the MINIMAL fix so that:
   - binding into `map[string][]string` works and yields all values for each key (no panic);
   - binding into `map[string]interface{}` yields the slice of values when a key has more than one value (and a plain string when it has exactly one — decide the most reasonable behavior consistent with how the code already behaves for single values, and document your choice in the report);
   - binding into `map[string]string` continues to work as before (single value per key);
   - existing struct binding, nested structs, slices, and all other binding paths are unchanged.
   Be careful to keep behavior for existing green tests identical.
3. Verify with a temporary throwaway test file (e.g. /echo/zz_bindmap_temp_test.go, package echo) covering at least: `?tag=a&tag=b` into map[string][]string -> {"tag":["a","b"]}; `?tag=a` into map[string][]string -> {"tag":["a"]}; `?tag=a&tag=b` into map[string]interface{}; `?tag=a` into map[string]string -> {"tag":"a"}; and a POST form with repeated fields. Delete the temp file afterwards.
4. Run the full suite: `cd /echo && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and compare with baseline — no previously passing test may fail. Run `go vet ./...`.
5. `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` must show only the source file(s) you intentionally changed (no temp files). Note: middleware/proxy.go and router.go were already modified by earlier work on other bugs — leave those alone.

REPORT BACK: exact diff, baseline vs post-fix test results, the choice you made for map[string]interface{} single-value behavior, and confirmation the temp file is deleted.

BUG TO FIX (reported by user): With the Gzip middleware enabled and a client sending `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, a handler that returns an EMPTY body with status 200 produces an inconsistent response: the body contains gzip bytes (starts with the gzip magic bytes 1f 8b) but the `Content-Encoding` header has been removed, so clients see garbage.

Reproduction:
```go
e := echo.New()
e.Use(middleware.Gzip())
e.GET("/empty", func(c echo.Context) error { return c.String(http.StatusOK, "") })
// request with header Accept-Encoding: gzip
```
EXPECTED (this is the spec to implement): the response must be a VALID, complete gzip stream AND must keep `Content-Encoding: gzip`, with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, so a client can gunzip it and get an empty body. I.e. status 200, Content-Encoding == "gzip", Content-Type contains "text/plain", and `gzip.NewReader(rec.Body)` must succeed and yield 0 bytes.

ROOT CAUSE (already analysed, verify it yourself): in `GzipWithConfig` (/echo/middleware/compress.go), the deferred cleanup does `if res.Size == 0 { delete Content-Encoding; res.Writer = rw; w.Reset(ioutil.Discard) }` then `w.Close()`. But `gzip.Writer.Write` flushes the 10-byte gzip header to the underlying writer even when called with an empty slice, so for an empty body the underlying response already contains gzip header bytes while `res.Size` is still 0. The cleanup then strips the Content-Encoding header and discards the rest of the stream, leaving orphan gzip bytes with no encoding header.

REQUIRED FIX (implement exactly this, minimal diff):
- Add a bool field to the `gzipResponseWriter` struct (place it last) recording that the underlying gzip writer has already been used / its header flushed to the response writer; set it in `(*gzipResponseWriter).Write` before calling `w.Writer.Write(b)`.
- In the deferred cleanup in `GzipWithConfig`, only do the "nothing was written" cleanup (delete Content-Encoding, `res.Writer = rw`, `w.Reset(ioutil.Discard)`) when `res.Size == 0` AND the gzip writer has NOT been started. When the gzip writer HAS been started but `res.Size == 0` (empty body written), keep `Content-Encoding: gzip` and let the existing `w.Close()` write the gzip trailer to the real response writer, producing a complete valid empty gzip stream. Note `grw` must be constructed before the deferred closure so it can be captured (the closure may reference it).
- Keep everything else identical: `w.Close()` and `pool.Put(w)` must still always run; the 204 No Content path (`gzipResponseWriter.WriteHeader` deleting Content-Encoding) and the error-returned path must behave exactly as before.

TASKS:
1. BEFORE any edit run `cd /echo && go test -count=1 ./middleware/ 2>&1 | tail -20` and save to /tmp/baseline_gzip.txt (note: another subagent may be editing other files; ignore failures unrelated to middleware/compress.go and record them).
2. Implement the fix in /echo/middleware/compress.go only.
3. Verify with a temporary throwaway test file /echo/middleware/zz_gzip_temp_test.go (package middleware) that must assert, for `e.Use(Gzip())` + `e.GET("/empty", func(c echo.Context) error { return c.String(http.StatusOK, "") })` and a request with `Accept-Encoding: gzip`: status 200; `rec.Header().Get(echo.HeaderContentEncoding) == "gzip"`; Content-Type contains `echo.MIMETextPlain`; `gzip.NewReader(rec.Body)` succeeds and reading it yields an empty string. Also assert the non-empty case still works (body "test" gunzips to "test", Content-Encoding gzip) and that a handler returning an error still yields no Content-Encoding. Run it and report the output. DELETE the temp file afterwards.
4. Run `cd /echo && go test -count=1 .

BUG TO FIX (reported by user): Registering two route groups with the SAME path prefix breaks the first group's routes.

Reproduction:
```go
e := echo.New()
g1 := e.Group("/group", m1)
g1.GET("", h)
g2 := e.Group("/group", m2)
g2.GET("/other", h)
```
Expected: `GET /group` runs h with m1, `GET /group/other` runs h with m2.
Actual: `GET /group` returns 404 (even though it was registered); only the second group's route works. Deleting the second group makes the first work again.

Relevant code: /echo/echo.go (func (e *Echo) Group), /echo/group.go (Group struct, Group.Group, Group.Add, Group.GET etc.), /echo/router.go (func (r *Router) Add). Note that the working tree already contains fixes for other bugs in middleware/proxy.go, router.go, context.go, bind.go — do NOT revert or modify those unrelated changes; only fix this group bug (likely in echo.go and/or group.go).

TASKS:
1. BEFORE any edit, run the baseline suite: `cd /echo && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and save to /tmp/baseline5.txt. Record baseline failures (only those may fail later).
2. Read /echo/echo.go `Group` and /echo/group.go fully. Find why the second group with the same prefix breaks the first group's route (look for middleware accumulation, `e.groups` bookkeeping, prefix handling, or how the route path is built). Implement the MINIMAL fix so that both groups work independently with their own middleware, and so that routes registered on a group are not affected by later groups with the same prefix.
3. Verify with a temporary throwaway test file (e.g. /echo/zz_group_temp_test.go, package echo) that: (a) the exact reproduction above gives 200 for `GET /group` (with m1 applied) and 200 for `GET /group/other` (with m2 applied); (b) each middleware only affects its own group's routes (e.g. middleware sets a header or a context value and you assert it is present/absent as expected); (c) a group with a different prefix still works; (d) nested groups (g.Group(...)) still work; (e) routes registered directly on Echo still work. Delete the temp file afterwards.
4. Run the full suite: `cd /echo && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and compare with baseline — no previously passing test may fail (group_test.go and echo_test.go must still pass). Run `go vet ./...`.
5. `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` must show only the source file(s) you intentionally changed (no temp files).

REPORT BACK: exact diff, root cause explanation, baseline vs post-fix test results, and confirmation the temp file is deleted.
